package.question: Does fine-tuning on self-generated concise reasoning (Method M) shorten LLM reasoning without reducing accuracy, compared with prompting and other fine-tuning approaches, and does the effect transfer across math datasets?
package.methods_summary: Method M is a self-training recipe for shorter chain-of-thought. For each training question, the model samples reasoning paths while conditioned on 8 concise few-shot exemplars (here written by GPT-4o), plus paths from its default distribution; the shortest correct path per question is kept, and the model is fine-tuned on these paths. Method M-FS samples a single few-shot-conditioned path instead of best-of-N. Baselines: zero-shot prompting (including an explicit 'be concise' instruction), fine-tuning on external reasoning (GPT-4o chain-of-thought), naive best-of-N self-training without exemplars (16 paths), and Rational Metareasoning.
package.experimental_setup: Five post-trained models (Llama-3.2-3B, Gemma-2-2B, Qwen2.5-3B, Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, DeepSeekMath-7B), fine-tuned separately for GSM8K and MATH; evaluation on the GSM8K test set and MATH500 with greedy decoding. Accuracy is parsed from final answers; length is the mean number of output tokens over all outputs, correct or not. Relative metrics divide by the zero-shot baseline prompt. Method M uses 16 few-shot-conditioned plus 16 default paths per question; the budget-matched variant uses 8 plus 8.
